title: Chase Zelle Payment Pending Review: Release Times & How to Clear It [2026]
content:
When sending funds through Chase QuickPay with Zelle, transactions are typically instantaneous. However, if your transfer status changes to **"Pending Review"** or **"Action Required,"** Chase’s automated risk mitigation engine has placed a temporary security hold on the payment.

This guide explains the exact triggers for Zelle security holds, how long funds remain in review, and the fastest steps to release your money.

## Why Does Chase Put Zelle Payments Under Review?

**Chase places Zelle payments under review when transactions deviate from normal account spending patterns, involve first-time recipients, or trigger fraud prevention algorithms.** The hold allows automated systems or risk analysts to verify that your account has not been compromised.

| Diagnostic Detail | Information |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Service** | Chase QuickPay with Zelle |
| **Typical Hold Duration** | 2 Hours to 48 Hours |
| **Status Labels** | "Pending Review", "Under Review", "Action Required" |
| **Risk Triggers** | High dollar value, new recipient, unusual login location |

> ⚠️ **Security Warning:** Beware of imposter scams! Scammers often send fake text messages claiming "Chase Fraud Alert: Did you send $500 via Zelle?" followed by a phone call asking for your OTP or password. Chase will NEVER ask you to read back a verification code over the phone.

## 6 Steps to Resolve and Clear a Pending Zelle Review

Follow these actionable steps to expedite the release of your funds:

### 1. Check Your Chase Secure Message Center
When Chase flags a payment, automated notifications are immediately sent to your internal banking inbox:
1. Log into the Chase mobile app or desktop website.
2. Tap the **Profile / Settings icon** and select **Secure Message Center**.
3. Look for messages titled **"Important information regarding your recent payment"**.
4. Follow the internal prompt to authorize or verify the transaction.

### 2. Look for Chase Fraud SMS Prompts
Chase typically sends an automated SMS alert from shortcode **24273**:
* The message will read: *"Did you attempt a Zelle payment of $X to [Recipient]? Reply YES or NO."*
* If you authorized the transfer, reply **YES**.
* Once confirmed, Chase will release the hold within 15–30 minutes or prompt you to re-submit the payment.

> 💡 **Related Chase Bank Solution:** Encountering related issues? Check our verified fix for [Chase Wire Transfer Status 'Action Required': Why It's Held & How to Clear It](/guides/chase-wire-transfer-status-action-required).


### 3. Check Outbound Daily and Monthly Zelle Limits
Attempting to send an amount that approaches or exceeds your account limit triggers mandatory secondary review:
1. In the Chase app, go to **Pay & Transfer** > **Zelle**.
2. Tap **Settings** > **Manage Daily Limits**.
3. Check your remaining daily allowance (most personal consumer accounts have a $2,000 to $5,000 daily limit, while business accounts have higher allowances).

### 4. Verify Recipient Enrollment Status
If the recipient has not linked their phone number or email address with a participating Zelle financial institution:
* The funds will remain in a pending state until the recipient registers with Zelle.
* If the recipient fails to enroll within **14 days**, the funds automatically return to your Chase checking balance.

### 5. Attempt to Cancel the Pending Payment
If the transfer is still under review and has not settled, you may have the option to revoke it:
1. Navigate to **Pay & Transfer** > **Zelle** > **Activity**.
2. Select the transaction marked **Pending Review**.
3. Look for a **Cancel Payment** button. If visible, tap it to immediately release the funds back to your available balance.

### 6. Call Chase Electronic Payments & Fraud Operations Directly
If 24 hours have passed without resolution, contact the dedicated risk team:
1. Call the official Chase customer service line: **1-800-935-9935**.
2. Request transfer to the **"Electronic Funds Transfer / Zelle Operations Department"**.
3. Provide the specific **Transaction ID** found in your payment activity receipt.

## Prevention Tips

To avoid future Zelle review delays:
* **Send a $1 Test Transaction:** When transferring funds to a new contact for the first time, send a nominal $1 transfer to establish account familiarity.
* **Avoid Public Wi-Fi When Initiating Transfers:** Submitting large peer-to-peer transfers from unfamiliar IP addresses flags fraud algorithms.
* **Confirm Your Phone Number:** Ensure your registered mobile phone number matches your carrier records.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

**Does "Pending Review" mean my money has been lost or stolen?**
**No.** A pending review simply means Chase has temporarily quarantined the transfer while verifying its legitimacy. The funds will either complete to the recipient or be returned to your account balance.

**How long can Chase legally hold a Zelle payment?**
**Most reviews conclude within 2 to 24 business hours.** However, if security analysts require verbal identity verification, the hold can extend up to 48 hours until you contact support.

**Can Chase reverse a Zelle payment once it completes?**
**No.** Once a Zelle payment status changes from "Pending" to "Completed," the transfer is irrevocable because Zelle transactions settle instantly between bank accounts.

**Will I be charged a fee for a cancelled Zelle payment?**
**No.** Chase does not charge any processing fees for sending, receiving, or cancelling Zelle transactions.
